zh.title: FAA發布通用航空活塞機隊轉用無鉛航空汽油過渡計畫
zh.summary: 美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）於2026年7月30日發布無鉛航空汽油過渡計畫，以分階段方式將無鉛燃料安全導入通用航空機隊，履行2024年FAA再授權法要求於2030年前完成活塞引擎機隊轉型的國會授權。FAA目前正於William J Hughes技術中心測試三種燃料，並透過EAGLE倡議與產業合作推進。
body: 美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）於2026年7月30日發布「無鉛航空汽油過渡計畫」，提供將無鉛燃料安全導入通用航空機隊的路線圖。該計畫採分階段方式，涵蓋燃料測試與授權、蒐集市場經驗、執行全國過渡，以及管理阿拉斯加的特殊過渡安排。
FAA署長Bryan Bedford表示，轉用無鉛燃料對通用航空社群及機場周邊居民均為正面進展，並強調此為涵蓋飛機製造商、燃料供應商、機場與飛行員的協同努力。
該計畫履行2024年FAA再授權法的一項條款，該條款要求FAA與航空產業合作，透過EAGLE（消除航空汽油鉛排放）倡議，於2030年前將活塞引擎機隊安全轉型為無鉛航空汽油。作為過渡第一階段的一環，FAA正於William J Hughes技術中心測試三種不同燃料，以釐清性能與相容性等關鍵問題，並將於第一階段完成後更新計畫。
FAA於2026年1月公布過渡計畫草案並徵詢公眾意見，機構運用這些意見改善並釐清最終計畫。FAA將於2026年稍晚發布的補充文件中摘要說明相關意見。

FAA與EAGLE利害關係人合作推動多項倡議，包括執行FAA活塞航空燃料倡議（PAFI）以支援LyondellBasell/VP Racing的UL100與Swift Fuels的100R的機隊授權；透過補充型別合格證（STC）途徑加速批准GAMI的G100UL與Swift Fuels的100R；並鼓勵機場引進無鉛燃料替代品的同時，要求在過渡期間維持100LL的供應。為防止推動過程中出現供應中斷，FAA將執行聯邦補助保證義務，確保機場在安全且廣泛可及的無鉛替代品到位前持續供應含鉛100LL。

en.title: FAA Releases Transition Plan for General Aviation Piston Fleet to Unleaded Aviation Gas
en.summary: On July 30, 2026, the FAA released its Transition Plan for Unleaded Aviation Gasoline, providing a phased roadmap to safely integrate unleaded fuel into the general aviation fleet. The plan fulfills a provision of the 2024 FAA Reauthorization Act requiring the agency to partner with industry through the EAGLE initiative to transition the piston-engine fleet to unleaded avgas by 2030. The FAA is testing three fuels at the William J Hughes Technical Center.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) released its Transition Plan for Unleaded Aviation Gasoline on July 30, 2026, providing a roadmap to safely integrate unleaded fuel into the general aviation fleet. The plan uses a phased approach to address fuel testing and authorization, gather market experience, execute the national transition, and manage the unique transition in Alaska.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the transition to unleaded fuel is a positive step forward for the general aviation community and people who live and work near general aviation airports, describing it as a collaborative effort involving aircraft manufacturers, fuel suppliers, airports, and pilots.

The plan fulfills a provision of the 2024 FAA Reauthorization Act requiring the agency to partner with the aviation industry to safely transition the piston-engine fleet to unleaded aviation gas by 2030. This partnership was carried out through the Eliminate Aviation Gasoline Lead Emissions (EAGLE) initiative. As part of the first phase, the FAA is testing three different fuels at the William J Hughes Technical Center to address key questions concerning performance and compatibility, and will update the plan after the first phase is complete.

In January 2026, the FAA published a draft of the transition plan and invited public comments. The agency used these comments to improve and clarify the final plan. The FAA will summarize the comments in a supplemental document that will publish in late 2026.

The FAA, in collaboration with EAGLE stakeholders, is leading several initiatives, including executing the FAA Piston Aviation Fuels Initiative (PAFI) to support Fleet Authorization for LyondellBasell/VP Racing's UL100 and the recent addition of Swift Fuels' 100R to PAFI. The FAA is also expediting the rollout of high-octane unleaded fuel by using the Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) pathway to approve GAMI's G100UL and Swift Fuels' 100R, while encouraging airports to introduce unleaded fuel alternatives and requiring the maintenance of 100LL availability through the transition. To prevent premature supply disruptions, the FAA is enforcing Federal Grant Assurance obligations to ensure airports continue to offer leaded 100LL until safe, fleet-wide unleaded alternatives are widely and locally accessible.
